bottom_line.headline: Eleven names cleared the committee into a RISK OFF tape: work them only on their hourly triggers, and decide MP before the open.
bottom_line.paragraph: The lists lean defensive (Healthcare, Staples, Financials, one Energy name), and every buy price sits just above Friday's high, so nothing is a buy on the open print. The index is in a downtrend below its short-term lines with dealers amplifying moves 2.12% under the SPY gamma flip, while the average stock keeps up with the index. MP is an exit case with the broker stop 36.66 as the only exit price; V is a keep with an add line at 414.60.

weather.stance: Read: Valen's stance is RISK OFF, unchanged from 5 days ago and down from NEUTRAL a month ago; SPY and QQQ fail both the daily and weekly buy signals and sit 1.52 and 2.71 ATRs below their 50-day lines, with VIX/VIX3M at 0.93, neither calm nor stressed. The handbook's doctrine for this reading is 'build the watchlist, do not push new entries', quoted as the VIV System's rule, not an Aegis sizing rule.
weather.gex: Read: the light is RED. SPY 755.72 sits 2.12% under the gamma flip at 771.76, so dealers amplify moves both ways; the put wall at 750 is the cushion just below, and losing it removes support, while reclaiming 771.76 (just past the 770 call wall) is what calms the tape. Not a knife-edge, and the dealer side is an assumption, not data.
weather.heartbeat: Read: breadth is broadening, the average stock keeping up with the index, for 10 days: RSP/SPY is up 1.38% over 5 days, 6.01% over 20 and 1.57% over 60, mid-range in its 12-month band (confidence 0.65, so the read is usable). The 20-day line 3.44% below is the line that would end it; the 12-month high 3.43% above is where a broadening run turns late.
weather.positioning: Read: trend funds are neutral across 18 markets, none at an extreme, size dial 1.00; they lean long the dollar (+0.43) and energy (+0.28), short rates (-0.40) and metals (-0.27). The nearest flips: they turn sellers if the Russell 2000 trades under 2,804.16 (0.61% away) and buyers of the 2-year above 103.20 (0.9% away); the small-cap line is the one that matters for a long book today.
weather.volatility: Read: VIX 19.42 is higher than 76% of days in the past two years, so not quiet; single-stock volatility of 42.3 leaves a gap of 22.88, in the normal band, flat over 20 days (+0.23) and just under the elevated band at 23.62. Implied correlation is low (13.51), so stocks trade on their own news and selection pays, the curve is in contango, and the dispersion cross-checks disagree, so treat the gap with caution.
weather.divergence: Read: one warning is lit at market level, momentum not keeping up with price, and 8 more showed on individual markets. Breadth is broadening, so it does not agree; on its own this is not a reason to sell.
weather.call: Read: Crown's family is BROADENING_CARRY at 1.00x the PM's own risk, a partial fit: the one condition that fails is dealers damping moves. The leading macro story is a dollar squeeze (75% of its conditions met, full coverage) but it is contested, with disinflation-goldilocks within 12%, so neither is a call; the next tests are ISM Manufacturing today at 10:00 ET and payrolls on Fri 6 Nov.
weather.cot: Read: large speculators are crowded long the Nasdaq 100, the Russell 2000, the 5-year and the 2-year notes, and crowded short crude, natural gas and silver (CFTC data to 27 Oct). The equity longs are the ones that matter: crowded Nasdaq and small-cap longs are what reverse fast if the 2,804.16 small-cap flip breaks; crowding is context, never timing.
weather.checklist: Read: on AQE's panel (US-listed, over $2B), net new highs pass (8-day 5.5 vs 20-day -2.6) and the 5-day 4% count is 1.00, right at the pass line; today's count is not green and monthly 25% risers number 58. The weak instruments are stocks above their 40-day line (42.7) and above their 50-day (37.5); these are AQE-list numbers, not the whole market.
weather.turning: Read: RISK OFF now and 5 days ago, NEUTRAL a month ago; the trend went from CHOP to DOWNTREND while stocks above their 40-day line improved from 29.7 to 39.3 to 42.7 and SPY slid from +0.14 to -1.09 to -1.52 ATRs against its 50-day. The stance turns up when stocks above their 40-day line clear 50 (now 42.7) and the 5-day 4% count clears 1.00; it turns down if that count falls under 0.70.
weather.themes: Read: the true leaders, strong on both horizons and near their highs, are Biotech (+7.23% week, +15.25% month, at its high), Insurance (1.21% off), Midstream MLP (2.64% off) and REITs (4.93% off). Oil Services, Infra Power, Infra Construction, Agri Commodities and Cloud Computing are bounces off the floor 15-25% under their highs, and the violent turns (Chip Equipment +30.89 thrust at 43.24% off its high, Quantum Computing, Crypto) are in broken groups: bounces, not leadership.
weather.groups: Read: the turning groups with strong names are Industrials (EFX, HAYW, LMT; FLYW and TTEK ride it), Financials (GPN, AJG, SPGI), Real Estate (CCI, CUBE) and Technology turning up from the bottom (BRZE, TENB, NTSK, DXC, GEN, all stretched). Healthcare, Staples, Energy, Utilities and Materials are already leading and further along; this is a place to look, not a list to buy.
